correctness.rationale: In a connected cubic graph with colored C and uncolored U, each U has all three neighbors colored, so 3|U|<=3|C|, and equality forces C,U bipartition classes. Connected cubic abelian Cayley graphs reduce to prisms and Möbius ladders (apart from small no-equality cases). Neighbor-triple constraints force a period-three color word on the colored shore, requiring m divisible by 6 for prisms or n≡6 mod12 for Möbius ladders; exactly 3!=6 per shore and two shores, hence 12. Both primary prior published papers reconstruct this exact count via their own all-order proofs. Inspected pinned graph-neighborhood enumeration source; finite tests are corroborative.

The broader connected cubic abelian Cayley statement follows by the classical prism/Möbius family classification. Matching count is a mathematical implication, not mere title overlap.
